Chapter 143: There’s an Anti-QQ Alliance?

On Xu Fengyin’s third day of work.

Inside a large classroom, Chen Guiliang was in the middle of a lecture when his phone suddenly vibrated.

Chen Guiliang took it out and looked. The text message read: "Come to the Science Park Innovation Center immediately. Someone from MSN China is here, planning to make an angel investment in Xiaonei Wang."

So soon?

And it shouldn't be MSN investing!

Chen Guiliang instinctively felt something was off. He replied to the text: "Tell them to wait. I have to attend class."

Over at the Innovation Center, Ao Yanchen wore a strange expression and sent back three question marks.

But Chen Guiliang did not text again.

Ao Yanchen forced himself to calm down and suddenly had a realization: this was President Chen's negotiation tactic. Yes, that must be it!

At this moment, inside Wang Kai's office, besides Ao Yanchen, there was also Du Zhe, an executive sent by MSN China.

Wang Kai chatted with Du Zhe for a while, then asked Ao Yanchen with a smile, "When will President Chen be able to come over?"

Ao Yanchen decided to execute Chen Guiliang's negotiation tactic: "President Chen said he has class and can't get away for now."

What the hell?

The smile on Wang Kai's face stiffened slightly.

This was MSN China, a subsidiary of a Microsoft subsidiary!

At a time like this, what class are you attending?

And you failed six courses last semester, and now you're telling me you need to study hard?

Wang Kai said to Du Zhe, the executive in charge of investments, "Mr. Du, that's just how Peking University students are. They are always completely focused when they study."

"It's no trouble," Du Zhe said with a smile. "An investment isn't something that can be negotiated in a matter of minutes. A delay of an hour or two is nothing."

Sitting to the side, Ao Yanchen was muttering to himself: I wonder how much the valuation will be for this angel investment. That bastard promised me stock options, he won't go back on his word at the last minute, will he?

Ao Yanchen probed, "Mr. Du, what is your valuation for Xiaonei Wang?"

"That will depend on Xiaonei Wang's detailed data," Du Zhe replied in a very formulaic manner. "Today is just a preliminary contact. If your company is willing to accept our investment, you will need to provide a business plan and other corresponding materials, which our professional team will then assess."

Ao Yanchen asked a few more things but didn't get much out of it.

Wang Kai said, "Mr. Du, would you like a tour of the Science and Technology Building? Our Science Park has many other innovative enterprises. Even if you only invest in Xiaonei Wang this time, you could still learn about the others. Perhaps there will be opportunities for collaboration in the future."

"No need to trouble yourself," Du Zhe directly refused.

The three of them just sat in the office, making small talk from time to time, patiently waiting for Chen Guiliang's class to end.

A full hour passed before Chen Guiliang finally arrived on his bicycle.

"President Chen, this is Mr. Du Zhe from MSN China."

"Hello, Mr. Du."

"Hello, Boss Chen."

The two shook hands and exchanged greetings. Wang Kai wanted to listen in.

Du Zhe said tactfully, "Manager Wang, could you arrange a small meeting room for us? Negotiating in your office might disturb your work."

"No problem." Wang Kai led them to a meeting room and had his subordinate send tea over.

In the small meeting room, only Chen Guiliang, Ao Yanchen, and Du Zhe remained.

Chen Guiliang was the first to voice his doubt, "MSN China is also in the venture capital business?"

Du Zhe smiled. "Not long ago, we acquired a telecom value-added service company in Shenzhen."

Chen Guiliang asked, "It seems the content of Xiaonei Wang competes with MSN Spaces, doesn't it?"

MSN Spaces offered blog, photo album, and list services. Its Chinese beta version had just launched a little over two months ago, competing with Xiaonei Wang's features like journals and photo albums.

Du Zhe said, "The users of MSN Spaces are mainly professionals in society, especially the elite white-collar class. Xiaonei Wang's users are students. The two can complement each other."

Chen Guiliang felt more and more that something was wrong. "What's your valuation for Xiaonei Wang, how much equity do you want, and what other requirements do you have for Xiaonei Wang? Let's be direct, don't beat around the bush."

Du Zhe chuckled, "President Chen is being a bit too hasty."

"It's just that Mr. Du's arrival is too unusual, it makes me feel uneasy," Chen Guiliang said truthfully. "I can't figure out what you guys are up to, so I'm not very keen on accepting the investment."

Du Zhe thought for a moment and said, "We plan to invest 500,000 US dollars for a 20% stake in Xiaonei Wang, and we will not interfere with its management. There is only one condition: Xiaonei Wang must join the Anti-QQ Alliance."

"What the hell?" Chen Guiliang thought he had misheard.

Since the news would be announced in a while anyway, Du Zhe decided to explain it directly. "Nine major websites, including Taobao, CCID, Mop, and Ourgame, have already formed an Anti-QQ Alliance with MSN China. All members of the Anti-QQ Alliance can receive user traffic support from MSN Messenger."

Chen Guiliang felt like laughing. Just how much did people hate QQ?

It was like they were forming a party to fight a boss.

Chen Guiliang asked, "If I join the Anti-QQ Alliance, what do I need to do?"

Du Zhe said:

"For Xiaonei Wang's user registration information, the option to fill in a QQ number will be removed. Only an MSN number can be filled in. Also, a channel will be built so that in the future, when Xiaonei Wang users enter the workforce, their accounts can be directly imported into MSN Spaces."

"That's about it. You just need to compete with QQ Zone for users. I'm afraid President Chen doesn't know yet that QQ is about to launch QQ Zone. The website is almost complete and will begin closed beta testing next month at the latest. Its functions are quite similar to your Xiaonei Wang!"

QQ's business scope was spread too wide, so it was only normal for it to attract animosity.

MSN China also had these services, but they found it difficult to build them up, so they roped in a bunch of allies to "outsource channels."

Among them, MSN's shopping channel was outsourced to Taobao. The operation of community and entertainment content was outsourced to Mop. IT and tech news services were outsourced to CCIDNet...

As for Xiaonei Wang and MSN Spaces, one focused on the student demographic and the other on the professional demographic. They could join forces to fight QQ Zone.

Furthermore, MSN China had a clever plan: they wanted to connect with Xiaonei Wang's user base. Xiaonei Wang's student users would be directly imported into MSN Spaces upon graduation, turning Xiaonei Wang into their user cultivation base.

The terms they offered were also quite tempting. Chen Guiliang would receive a sum of angel investment, and Xiaonei Wang would gain user traffic from MSN Messenger.

It seemed to be a mutually beneficial arrangement.

The plan looked beautiful, but the execution was a pile of crap.

For such a grand and vast plan, Microsoft and MSN headquarters had only allocated 5 million US dollars to MSN China, telling them to raise the rest of the funds themselves.

Moreover, the vast majority of MSN China's decisions and applications had to be reported up through the layers of Microsoft's global system. The only contracts they could approve on their own were for projects under 500,000 US dollars.

In other words, the most MSN China could invest in Xiaonei Wang was 500,000 US dollars. If the amount exceeded that, it would have to be reported to Microsoft headquarters, and the approval process would take over a year, possibly even two!

Chen Guiliang asked, "500,000 US dollars for 20% of my company. Does Mr. Du think that's possible?"

Du Zhe tried to sweet-talk him, "President Chen, you can't just look at the money. With a 500,000-dollar angel investment from Microsoft, it will instill confidence in other investors, and Xiaonei Wang's value could skyrocket instantly. Besides, Xiaonei Wang will also get user traffic from MSN Messenger. It will also help improve Xiaonei Wang's image. After all, we are MSN, not a low-quality communication tool like QQ."

This statement almost made Chen Guiliang laugh out loud.

Apart from the "value skyrocketing" part being correct, everything else was utter nonsense.

And Du Zhe didn't even think he was talking nonsense, because he genuinely looked down on QQ.

At this time, in the Chinese instant messaging market, QQ held a 77.8% share, while MSN held 10.87%.

However, among the roughly 20 million Chinese business professionals, there were 10.75 million MSN users, compared to only 9.5 million QQ users. Furthermore, most of the high-level executives among these professionals used MSN.

This situation gave people a false impression that MSN was high-end, sophisticated, and classy, while QQ was low-end, vulgar, and crude.

It wasn't just business professionals; even many students thought this way.

They were proud to have an MSN account and ashamed to use QQ for communication.

It had even formed into a social sentiment, with the media widely predicting QQ's downfall.

From Microsoft to MSN headquarters, and all the way down to MSN China, everyone believed that taking down QQ was only a matter of time!

Chen Guiliang said, "Mr. Du, I appreciate that you think highly of Xiaonei Wang. But if the valuation is less than 5 million US dollars, I don't think there's any need to continue this discussion. Moreover, Xiaonei Wang's user base is still surging. The next time we talk, it might not be a matter of 5 million US dollars anymore."

"President Chen won't reconsider?" Du Zhe asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Your side is the one that needs to reconsider. I still have class, so I won't keep you company."

"Alright then, I'll go back and discuss it." Du Zhe stood up and shook hands with Chen Guiliang.

The man was quite polite. Before leaving, he made a point to say goodbye to Wang Kai.

Wang Kai repeatedly urged him to stay, but Du Zhe politely declined.

"How did it go?" Wang Kai came back and asked Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang said, "Their offer was too low, and their demands were too high. I refused."

Wang Kai didn't ask for details, as it would be useless. He merely expressed his regret.

As Chen Guiliang was heading back to the company with Ao Yanchen, he said while waiting for the elevator, "Don't you have anything to say?"

"Would it make a difference what I say?" Ao Yanchen retorted.

Chen Guiliang said, "MSN China is too petty. It's destined to fail."

In fact, it wasn't that they were petty, but that their headquarters gave them too little authority. And it would only get tighter and tighter. If MSN China wanted to add a new feature, they had to go through layers of applications and approvals. By the time it was approved, the opportunity would be long gone.

This ultimately led to QQ's user experience leaving MSN in the dust by a country mile!

Chen Guiliang said, "Contact Tencent. Tell them MSN approached us to form an alliance against QQ. See if we can squeeze something out of Tencent."

"What more do you want to get out of Tencent?" Ao Yanchen asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "They should at least give me a 5-digit QQ number, right?"

Ao Yanchen, rendered utterly speechless, added, "I want one too."

This year was a very special one for China's internet industry.

Douban, Tudou, 56.com, Qunar, PPTV, 58.com... were all founded one after another. In another timeline, Xiaonei Wang and 5Q Campus Network were also born this year.

The second spring of the internet industry had arrived!

Last month, when Chen Guiliang was blasting "Wolf Totem," Shanda's president, Tang Jun, walked into Boss Chen's office and said, "Let's make our move tonight."

The next day, Shanda announced that it had acquired a 19.5% stake in Sina from the Nasdaq open market. Shanda was now Sina's largest shareholder.

Simultaneously with the announcement, Boss Chen called Sina's CEO, Wang Yan, who knew nothing about it.

Sina was forced to activate its poison pill plan.

Shanda wanted to swallow the poison pill, but lacked sufficient funds, so Tang Jun pulled Yahoo into the fray.

The result of Tang Jun's negotiation with Yahoo was this: Yahoo headquarters would invest 1 billion US dollars in Shanda, and Shanda would acquire Yahoo China. With this 1 billion dollars, Shanda would complete its acquisition of Sina. But for the next three to five years, Yahoo headquarters would have controlling rights over Shanda.

Boss Chen was unwilling to give up control and flatly refused to sign.

The 1 billion US dollars that Boss Chen rejected was, a few months later, injected into a cash-strapped Alibaba...

Tang Jun would later complain often: "If Chen Tianqiao had signed back then, there would be no Alibaba!"

This year was a confluence of momentous events, with far-reaching consequences.

And now there was Chen Guiliang, a troublemaker, who managed to get Tencent's Pony Ma on the phone and said right off the bat, "I want ten 5-digit QQ numbers."

(End of Chapter)
